items.definition:
an electronic cigarette
He bought a new vape at the store.

something that goes with something else
The piano provided a beautiful accompaniment to the singer's voice.

a person who helps another commit a crime
The thief's accomplice waited in the getaway car.

a minor illness
He suffered from a minor ailment that kept him home from work.

an agreement made by opposing sides in a war to stop fighting for a certain time; a truce
The two countries signed an armistice to end the conflict.

a place where weapons are kept
The old armory was converted into a museum.

a salt of carbonic acid
Calcium carbonate is a common mineral found in rocks.

the arrangement of events or dates in the order of their occurrence
The historian established a clear chronology of events.

customers, clients
The restaurant has a loyal clientele.

skilled worker
The table was made by a master craftsman.

the state of being curved
The curvature of the Earth is visible from space.

place where spirits are made
We visited a whisky distillery in Scotland.

the act of arranging documents
She spent the afternoon doing paperwork and filing.

a defensive player in sports
The fullback made a great tackle.

a device for measuring
The pressure gage showed a high reading.

a kitchen on a ship or aircraft
The chef prepared meals in the ship's galley.

a man who is insane or behaves in a wild, reckless way
The villain in the movie was portrayed as a madman.

a person exhibiting extreme symptoms of wild behavior, especially when violent and dangerous
He drove like a maniac on the highway.

merchandise (informal)
They were selling band merch at the concert.

the study of weather and climate
Meteorology helps us understand weather patterns.

a mistaken idea or belief
Many people have a misconception about how the system works.

a priest or military chaplain
The soldiers often sought advice from the padre.

a person or organization that pays money
The insurance company is the primary payer for medical expenses.

a cunning plan or scheme
It was a clever ploy to distract the guards.

an idea taken to be true, or arrogant behavior
His presumption of innocence was challenged by the evidence.

a very tall coniferous tree
California is famous for its giant redwood trees.

deep respect for someone or something
The students showed great reverence for their wise teacher.

the quality or state of being selfish
His selfishness prevented him from sharing his toys.

a member of the armed forces
The serviceman returned home after a long deployment.

a person regarded as having access to, and influence in, the world of good and evil spirits
The shaman performed a ritual to heal the sick.

a small amount of liquid ejected
He gave the plant a squirt of water.

an act of stopping or being stopped
There was a temporary stoppage of work due to a power cut.

a nation with a very powerful military and economy; an exceptional ability
The United States is considered a global superpower.

a slight smell; a brief, faint indication
I caught a whiff of freshly baked bread.

a plant disease causing wilting; a loss of vigor
The flowers showed signs of wilt after a week without water.

the highest class in certain societies, typically holding hereditary titles or offices
The aristocracy once held significant power in many European countries.

an accumulation of tasks unperformed or materials not processed
We have a huge backlog of orders to process after the holiday sale.

expensive, ostentatious jewelry or accessories
He likes to show off his new car and all its bling.

the quality of someone's character or ability; the internal diameter of a gun barrel
The new recruits are of a very high calibre.

the dead body of an animal
The vultures circled above the animal carcass.

a person who conquers a place or people
William the Conqueror invaded England in 1066.

a point or limit at which something is stopped or reduced
The cutoff date for applications is next Friday.

a general statement or concept obtained by inference from specific cases
It's dangerous to make a generalization about an entire group of people.

a foolish, stupid, or clumsy person; a thug or ruffian
The security guard looked like a big goon, but he was actually very kind.

a person living in solitude
The old man lived like a hermit in the mountains.

a tree or shrub with large, showy flowers
The magnolia tree in the garden is blooming beautifully.

remote, sparsely inhabited inland regions of Australia
They traveled deep into the Australian outback.

a strong public expression of protest or disapproval
There was a public outcry against the new policy.

an orange-yellow spice derived from the crocus flower
Saffron is the most expensive spice in the world.

something that slides or is slid
The baseball player was a good slider into home plate.

a person who suffers from something
She is a long-time sufferer of chronic pain.

the quality of being appropriate
We need to assess the suitability of the candidate for the role.

a belief not based on reason
Breaking a mirror is considered a bad luck superstition.

a habitual spasmodic contraction of the muscles
He developed a nervous tic in his eye.

a person who travels on foot; the sound of heavy steps
We heard the tramp of heavy boots approaching.

a semiconductor device
Transistors are fundamental components in modern electronics.

the quality of being unique
The uniqueness of her artwork made it stand out.

a bone forming part of the spinal column
He fractured a vertebra in his lower back.

the quality of being acid
The acidity of the soil affects plant growth.

a natural ability to do something
She showed a natural aptitude for learning languages.

something or someone that obstructs or prevents movement
The defender was an excellent blocker on the field.

a sudden burst or failure; an overwhelming victory
The team won by a complete blowout.

a disappointing or unpleasant situation
It's a real bummer that the concert was canceled.

the mechanism of a clock; regular and precise operation
The train arrived like clockwork every day.
